samples.summary: New login-page error banner (`?error=login_state` → message, plus unknown-code fallback) has no test anywhere in the frontend suite
samples.evidence: `LoginForm` gains a `useSearchParams()` read and a conditional `role="alert"` banner driven by `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR`. This is the user-facing half of the backend's new `res.redirect('.../login?error=login_state')` path (auth.controller.ts:211), and it is the only thing a person sees when a browser callback is refused. Globbing `packages/frontend/src/**/*login*` returns only the component itself; grepping for `login-form`/`LoginForm` across the repo finds no spec/test file. The frontend vitest lane runs, so a test was possible. Neither the mapped message, the fallback for an unknown `error` value, nor the no-error (banner absent) case is asserted.

samples.summary: The `logSafeUrl` wiring into pino's `req` serializer is untested — only the pure function is covered
samples.evidence: `log-safe-url.spec.ts` exercises `logSafeUrl` thoroughly as a unit, but nothing asserts that the access-log serializer actually calls it: a revert of the one-line change at app.module.ts:70 (`url: logSafeUrl(req.url)` back to `url: req.url`) leaves every test in the diff green while re-parking OAuth `code`/`state` in the log. Grepping `logSafeUrl` finds only log-safe-url.ts, its spec, app.module.ts and docs — no module/integration test.

samples.summary: Consent-page test does not assert the continue link carries `nonce` and `code_challenge`, the two params that make the resumed CLI start valid
samples.evidence: The only consent-page assertions are `html` contains `http://127.0.0.1:9876`, `cli_confirm=tok-123`, and `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876`. `renderCliConsent` (auth.controller.ts:145-151) also puts `nonce` and `code_challenge` into the href; dropping either would make the guard reject the confirmed start with `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce')` and break every real CLI login, yet no test in this diff would fail. The guard spec drives the confirmed start with a hand-built query rather than the rendered page, so nothing checks the handoff.

samples.summary: New `codeVerifier` DTO validation (`@IsOptional @IsString @Length(43,128)`) is never exercised; controller specs call the handler directly with an out-of-range value
samples.evidence: auth.controller.spec.ts:676 passes `codeVerifier: 'nope'` (4 chars) — an input the real `ValidationPipe` would reject with 400 before the controller ran — so the 'burns a challenged code even when the verifier is wrong' test asserts on an unreachable production input. No test constructs/validates `CliExchangeDto` itself, so a wrong bound (or a dropped `@IsOptional`, which would break pre-PKCE clients) is uncovered.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s TTY branch is untested, and the file branch's test silently depends on the ambient `process.stderr.isTTY` being falsy
samples.evidence: login.ts:212 branches on `process.stderr.isTTY`; the TTY branch prints the authorization URL (nonce + challenge) to stderr. packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:256-262 asserts `notices.some(n => n.includes('nonce='))` is false and that the URL was written to `urlPath` — both only hold on the non-TTY branch, and grepping `isTTY` under packages/cli shows the login test never stubs `process.stderr.isTTY`. Run under a TTY the assertions describe different behavior, and the printed-URL path (and the third `catch` branch that prints the 'could not write' advice) has no coverage at all.

samples.summary: `codeForStatus`'s HTTP_ERROR row (exit 1) is untested; only the 401→UNAUTHORIZED and 5xx→SYSTEM rows are driven
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts covers a 401 exchange (`exit:2`, code UNAUTHORIZED) and a 502 workspaces call (`exit:2`, code SYSTEM). No test drives a 4xx that is not 401/403, so the third branch — `HTTP_ERROR` with `process.exit(1)` — and the exit-code split it encodes are unexercised.

samples.summary: 'stores no CLI state for a non-CLI request' asserts something trivially true for the web path
samples.evidence: `store.consumeState(web.__oauthState)` is called with a `w.`-prefixed HMAC string that was never a store key, so `undefined` comes back regardless of guard behavior on the web path — the assertion cannot distinguish a correct guard from one that, say, minted the web state wrongly. The out-of-range-port half of the same test is meaningful; the non-CLI half is not, and nothing else asserts that a non-CLI request leaves the CLI store empty (e.g. by checking store size or by asserting the state token has the web prefix).

samples.summary: The `InternalServerErrorException('Cannot start a login session')` path when the response cannot set cookies has no test
samples.evidence: `issueLoginCookie` throws when `res.cookie` is not a function — a deliberate fail-fast added in this diff. Every context built by `contextFor` in github-auth.guard.spec.ts supplies a `cookie` function, so the guard branch at line 288-290 is never entered by any test.

The mock `configService` only ever returns `http://localhost:5173` (no trailing slash), so the `.replace(/\/$/, '')` and the empty-`FRONTEND_URL` fallback in `loginErrorUrl` are never exercised; the redirect assertions would pass with the normalization removed.

samples.summary: `escapeHtml` is only incidentally covered by the `&` in the query separator; quote/angle-bracket escaping is untested
samples.evidence: The single consent-page test asserts `/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876`, which exercises only the `&` replacement. No test feeds a `nonce`, `confirmToken` or path containing `"`, `<`, `>` or `'` through `renderCliConsent`, so the remaining four replacements (and the `self` path interpolation, which is not URL-encoded before escaping) have no coverage.

samples.summary: The `sawUnboundCode` timeout message branch is untested
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` records `sawUnboundCode` when a callback arrives with no `state` and swaps the timeout error for a diagnostic about an older backend. login-callback.test.ts hits the 400 response for a stateless callback but never lets the 30-second timeout fire, so the branch that turns that flag into a message is uncovered (no fake timers used in the file).
